    Nearly-Extinct Cohort Methods

    nec.Rd

    Estimate population stocks of nearly-extinct cohorts using the Survivor Ratio (SR), Das Gupta (DG), or Survivor Ratio Advanced (SA) method. See vignette for an example.

    nec(
  y,
  x,
  d,
  yb = NULL,
  alpha = NULL,
  method = c("SR", "DG", "SA"),
  k = 5,
  m = 5,
  n = 10,
  min_age = 85,
  omega = NULL
)

    Arguments

    y

    Numeric vector. Calendar year.

    x

    Numeric vector. Age in the Lexis square.

    d

    Numeric vector. Deaths in the Lexis square.

    yb

    Numeric vector (optional). Year of birth. If NULL, cohort deaths are obtained by splitting each square using alpha.

    alpha

    Numeric scalar in between 0 and 1. Upper-triangle share. Default 0.5.

    method

    Character. "SR", "DG", or "SA".

    k

    Number of years over which survivor ratios are calculated. Used by SR and SA. Default 5.

    m

    Number of older cohorts used to estimate survivor/death ratios. Default 5.

    n

    Number of older cohorts used to estimate survival improvement in SA. Default 10.

    min_age

    Youngest age to estimate. Default 85.

    omega

    Extinction age. Cohorts aged omega or older at the calculation date are assumed extinct. Default is max observed age + 1.

    Value

    A data frame with yb, x, y and estimated population pop.

    Details

    Deaths are first assigned to cohorts from Lexis triangles. The method estimates the population remaining at the end of the observed death series; earlier population stocks are then reconstructed backwards by adding observed cohort deaths.

    References

    Terblanche, W. and Wilson, T. (2015). An Evaluation of Nearly-Extinct Cohort Methods for Estimating the Very Elderly Populations of Australia and New Zealand. PLoS ONE 10(4): e0123692.
